story.headline: Domains were the beginning. Not the boundary.
home: Lucky Domains began with domain acquisition, because names and ownership matter. The work grew from there: the website built on the name, the search visibility that brings people to it, and the entity and authority signals that help search engines and AI systems understand the brand.
Domains are still part of the business. They are now one part of a broader digital presence.
about: Lucky Domains started as a domain practice: finding the right name, valuing it honestly, reaching an owner who never listed it for sale, and closing through escrow. Names and ownership matter, and that work continues.

A name needs a site worth putting on it. A site needs to be found. And being found increasingly means being understood, first by search engines that organize the web around entities, and now by AI systems that answer questions directly.

So the work expanded in the order a presence is built: domain, website, search, entity, AI. Today Lucky Domains is a digital presence studio for the AI era, based in Berkeley Heights, New Jersey, and still run by its founder.

aiWork.title: AI-powered execution. Human accountability.
aiWork.intro: AI and internal automation handle the slow, repetitive parts of the job, which adds speed and depth. Ken stays responsible for the work, the decisions, and the quality, and reviews every recommendation before it reaches you.
uses: The questions customers ask, and who answers them now.
Page drafts and repetitive markup move faster. Every change is tested before it ships.
Indexing, speed, and crawlability checked across every page.
Page maps built from real search demand.
Markup checked against the visible facts.
Every profile and listing that describes a brand, and where they disagree.
Indexing, queries, and cited sources tracked over time.
Links, metadata, accessibility, and performance checked on every change.
aiWork.example: An example from our own operations: the Autonomous SEO Agent is an internal system that researches listing sites and creates profiles each day. It is not a client product, and no SEO impact has been established.
aiWork.limit: Client work is never left to run on its own. AI is how the work gets done, not a service we sell.

experience: Roughly two decades across accounting, financial reporting, and project, product, and program leadership at S&P Global, EY, Noom, and Prudential Financial, where he served as Director of Project and Product Management.

check.title: Digital Presence Check
check.lead: Ten questions about your domain, website, search visibility, identity, and AI visibility. It takes about two minutes and points to areas worth a closer look.

websites.title: What we look at
websites.lead: The same checks apply whether we review the site you have or build a new one.
items: Information architecture
One page per job, organized the way customers search.
Navigation
Every important page reachable from the homepage in two clicks.
Responsive design
Templates that work on every screen size, starting with phones.
Accessibility
Semantic markup, keyboard support, readable contrast, and motion that respects user settings.
Page performance
Fast templates, compressed images, and nothing loaded that the page does not need.
Canonical URLs
One address per page, with internal links and the sitemap in agreement.
Structured data
Organization, Person, and service data that matches the visible text.
Forms
Clear paths to contact that work with a keyboard alone.
Maintainability
A site you can edit without us, documented in plain English.

seo.title: What we look at
seo.lead: An audit reads the site the way a search engine does, then the way a customer does.
items: Crawlability
Whether search engines can reach every important page, with nothing important blocked.
Indexing
Which pages are indexed, which are not, and why.
Internal linking
Links that point to canonical URLs and show which pages matter.
Search intent
Whether each page targets one clear thing a searcher is trying to do.
Technical errors
Broken links, redirect chains, duplicate URLs, and slow templates.
Content structure
Titles, headings, and copy that answer the question the page is for.
Local search signals
Google Business Profile, consistent listings, and reviews, for businesses that serve a place.
Search Console data
Queries, coverage, and changes over time, read before anything is changed.

ai.title: What we look at
ai.lead: The work starts with what AI systems say today, and what they base it on.
items: Brand-related queries
The questions people ask about your business and your category.
AI-generated descriptions
How major AI assistants describe the business today, and whether it is accurate.
Source and citation patterns
Which sources those answers lean on, and where your brand is missing or misdescribed.
First-party content quality
Whether your own pages say who you are, what you do, where, and for whom.
Important unanswered questions
Questions a customer would ask that nothing on your site answers.
External authority signals
Credible third-party references that corroborate what you say about yourself.

entity.title: What we look at
entity.lead: Identity work compares what you say about yourself, in words and in data, everywhere you say it.
items: Organization and Person structured data
Markup with stable identifiers that describes real, visible facts.
Identity consistency
The same name, logo, and description everywhere.
Official profiles
Links to official profiles only, and profiles that link back.
Founder relationships
Founder, company, and author relationships stated in plain words and in data.
Canonical entity home
One page that says, authoritatively, who you are.
Entity disambiguation
What separates you from people and companies with similar names.

domains.title: What the work involves
domains.lead: Every acquisition follows the same order, and nothing is contacted before the range is set.
items: Ownership research
Who owns the name, for how long, and any obvious trademark conflict.
Valuation
A fair-market range from comparable sales, traffic, and strategic value.
Acquisition strategy
Whether to approach the owner, wait, backorder, or choose an alternative.
Outreach
Anonymous contact, so the price reflects the name and not the buyer.
Negotiation
Against the range you agreed, not the seller's opening ask.
Transfer and escrow
Escrow terms agreed before any money moves, and a verified transfer.

websites.title: How our own sites are built
websites.body: LuckyDomains.io moved from Wix to plain static HTML on the company's own domain: one canonical URL per page, 93 internal links rewritten to match, and a test suite that runs on every change. The decisions are public. On KenAshe.ai, Ken's own site, 2,083 PNG images were migrated to WebP with responsive images.
websites.note: Our own sites, not client work. No traffic, ranking, or lead figures are claimed.
links: Image pipeline build record on KenAshe.ai

seo.title: An internal system: the Autonomous SEO Agent
seo.body: Lucky Domains runs an internal agent that researches listing sites, creates profiles, and confirms its own verification emails each day. So far it has researched 63 sites and confirmed 8 profiles live. Most of those profiles carry nofollow links, and no SEO impact has been established.
seo.note: An internal system, shown to illustrate how automation supports research and monitoring. Not a client product and not a client result.

entity.title: The founder's own identity
entity.body: Ken Ashe's Person data uses one stable identifier on both KenAshe.ai and LuckyDomains.io, with 19 profile references and four professional credentials described in structured data.
entity.note: The founder's own sites, not client work. Google creates Knowledge Panels on its own, and no panel is claimed here.
links: See the structured data in the page source of LuckyDomains.io

carry.title: What an identity for an agent would need to carry
carry.intro: Whatever the naming system, the same handful of jobs keep coming up.
items: A human-readable name
Something a person can read, say, and remember.
Ownership
A clear record of who controls the name.
Discovery
A known place to look the agent up.
Machine-readable service information
What the agent does and how to call it, in a form other software can read.
A wallet and a payment destination
Somewhere to be paid that is tied to the same name.
Provenance
Evidence that a result really came from that agent.
Reputation
A record that travels with the name.

check.statement: This is a preliminary self-check, not a technical audit.
check.privacy: Nothing you select is stored or sent. The check runs entirely in your browser.

groups.name: Domain
groups.advice: Confirm who controls the registration, and whether the name still fits the brand.
questions: We control the domain our business runs on, in an account the business owns.
You do not need an exact-match domain. You need a suitable one that you control.
The domain is easy to say and spell, and our email uses it.
A name people can repeat, and the same name on your email, both build trust.

groups.name: Website
groups.advice: A written review of structure, clarity, speed, and the mobile experience is the usual first step.
questions: Within a few seconds, a new visitor can tell what we do, who we serve, and how to reach us.
Clarity comes before design.
The site loads quickly and works well on a phone.
Many first visits happen on a phone.

groups.name: Search
groups.advice: Check indexing and Search Console before changing any content.
questions: We appear in search results when someone searches for our business name.
If your own name does not find you, something basic is in the way.
We appear for the main services we offer, in the places we serve.
This is how people who do not know your name yet find you.

groups.name: Identity
groups.advice: Put your name, description, and profiles side by side, then look at the structured data on your site.
questions: Our name, description, and contact details match across our website and official profiles.
When sources disagree, search engines and AI systems hesitate.
Our website includes Organization or Person structured data that matches what the page says.
If you are not sure, that is common. It is quick to check.

groups.name: AI visibility
groups.advice: Ask the AI assistants your customers use how they describe you, and note which sources they cite.
questions: We have checked how AI assistants describe our business.
A few minutes with the assistants your customers use is enough to start.
When AI assistants describe us, the description is accurate.
Choose Not sure if you have not checked yet.

check.allYes: Nothing was flagged by these ten questions. That does not mean there are no problems. A self-check cannot see what a technical review would.
check.nojs: With JavaScript off, the check cannot total your answers. Each area below still links to the service that covers it.
